principles: Minimize behavioral change: preserve the existing validation entrypoint priority order.
Make the requirement mechanically traceable from truth source to implementation and smoke evidence.
Fail closed for configured validation command failures while treating missing entrypoint as explicit warn/skip policy.
Keep this story scoped to the single high gap and avoid unrelated medium fixture debt.
drivers: Current convergence_check is blocked by one high uncovered requirement.
testing-infra.md requires cross-language projects without configured validators to avoid false failures.
Validation framework changes are high risk because they affect TEST/DONE confidence.

options.name: A: Add exact policy annotation and focused smoke cases
pros: Smallest change that closes the mechanical coverage gap.
Proves both no-entry warn/skip and configured hard-fail behavior.
Avoids touching lifecycle gates or validation executor internals.
cons: Does not redesign validation detector registry or address medium legacy fixture gaps.

options.name: B: Refactor validation entrypoint selection into a dedicated registry
pros: Could make future validation detector changes clearer.
May align with broader lifecycle registry direction.
cons: Too large for the current single high gap.
Higher regression risk in validation flow and doctor output.
Would delay convergence closure without new behavioral requirement.

options.name: C: Change documentation wording to match current implementation
pros: Fastest apparent way to remove ambiguity.
cons: Would weaken the truth source instead of proving implementation coverage.
Does not add smoke evidence for no-entry warn/skip or configured hard-fail.

chosen: A: Add exact policy annotation and focused smoke cases
rationale: Choose the smallest implementation-backed closure: add a precise @task policy back-link in verifier.ts and smoke tests for the two missing validation semantics. This resolves the high gap without expanding into unrelated registry or fixture debt.

preMortem.scenario: The annotation closes the text gap but attaches to the wrong function scope and creates a new medium no-test gap.
preMortem.trigger: Adding function-level @task without a matching fixture-style @test annotation.
preMortem.consequence: convergence_check still fails or gap_analyze reports fresh medium debt from this story.
preMortem.mitigation: Use a file-level verifier policy annotation and rely on validation-protocol-smoke plus checklist evidence for test proof.

preMortem.scenario: No-entry warn/skip accidentally masks configured validation failures.
preMortem.trigger: Test only checks no-entry status and not configured failure behavior.
preMortem.consequence: Projects with explicit strong gates could pass despite failing validate.command(s).
preMortem.mitigation: Add configured command failure smoke asserting provider configured, status fail, allPass false, command exit code captured, and no fallback wording.

preMortem.scenario: Smoke tests become flaky because fallback discovery finds commands from parent/current repo state.
preMortem.trigger: Temporary roots inherit config cache or contain marker files that trigger package/python/go fallback detection unintentionally.
preMortem.consequence: No-entry test fails locally or in CI with environment-dependent provider/status.
preMortem.mitigation: Use isolated mkdtemp roots, call resetConfigCache before each verifier invocation, and create only the files required for each case.
